\begin{table}[htbp]

  \caption{Reliability of the Verifier's confidence blend on the hotpotqa calibration slice: ECE $=$ 0.332 over 10 equal-width bins, MCE $=$ 0.636, Brier $=$ 0.339 against a base-rate baseline of 0.224 (skill -0.510). The signal is \emph{not} well calibrated as a probability, so the threshold must be read as a ranking cut-point rather than as a probability of correctness. Discrimination is a separate question from calibration: AUC $=$ 0.633, i.e.\ the confidence ranks a correct answer above an incorrect one that often. The ordering is informative even though the scale is not, so a threshold on it is meaningful as a cut-point. An empty bin renders as a zero count and a \texttt{--} accuracy, never as an accuracy of zero.}
